messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Multilevel CFA w/Ordered Categorical Indicators + WLSMV Estimation
parts: Is there a way to conduct multilevel CFA with ordered categorical indicators and WLSMV estimation in lavaan?

lavaan does handle some basic multilevel situations (only 2-level models with complete data, no random slopes)

http://users.ugent.be/~yrosseel/lavaan/zurich2017/MULTILEVEL/lavaan_multilevel_zurich2017.pdf

Only in the development version.  See how to install:

http://lavaan.ugent.be/development.html

But no categorical variables at this point.

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Multilevel CFA w/Ordered Categorical Indicators + WLSMV Estimation
parts: In Mplus, you can use sampling weights to compute standard errors and the chi-square test statistic to account for clustered data. Is there a similar function in lavaan for ordered categorical data with WLSMV estimation?

The survey package can adjust for clustering, stratification, and sampling weights, and the lavaan.survey package provides an easy way to pass information to/from the lavaan and survey packages to get robust SEs for your SEMs.  Unfortunately, the survey package does not provide the tools to deal with categorical outcomes.

How many categories are there?  Some research indicates robust MLE  (e.g., estimator = "MLM") should yield sufficiently unbiased results when there are at least 5-7 categories, depending on how asymmetric the thresholds are.  But they only investigated regular CFA, not multilevel CFA.

http://psych.colorado.edu/~willcutt/pdfs/Rhemtulla_2012.pdf

If you have several items per factor, parceling would also be provide a way to items with more categories and therefore more likely for MLE to work.  But I do not recommend parceling if your research questions are about the measurement model itself.  Even if your research questions are about the structural level, you should take great care in how you allocate items to parcels in a theory-driven way:

https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC3909043/

or to take uncertainty into account if you allocate parcels randomly.  See the references on the ?parcelAllocation help page in the semTools package for more information.
